findings.summary: tolO does not tell o from an all-zero output on the test's own data (every sampled element at D=128, 88-100% at D=64), is ~1e4 on benchmark data at D=128 and ~1e6 at N=2^16
findings.detail: I evaluated Post's tolO (Model.lean's constants, transcribed in work/tolerance.py) on data drawn as the host draws it, at each row's own X = max_j sigma*scoreAbs(n, j), the smallest X Post allows (work/tolerance.out). (1) The test's data (normal(0, 0.5) in float16 cast to float8e5, sm_scale = 0.5, test_op's fwd shapes): at HEAD_DIM = 128 the median tolO is 0.53 to 1.02 against a median |attnRef| of 0.013 to 0.089, and the output 0 meets Post (|0 - attnRef| <= tolO) on 100% of the sampled elements in all six configurations (N_CTX 128, 1024, 4096, causal or not); at HEAD_DIM = 64 on 88% to 100%. So on its own test inputs Post does not reject a kernel that writes zeros (the failure this kernel has on its heads without vIn), nor one that flips the sign or drops sm_scale. Part of this is fp8 itself: a floor bound that keeps only the two fp8 roundings the kernel cannot avoid (p.to(float8e5) and the output's, 1/8 each, everything else exact) also admits 0 on long non-causal rows; but at HEAD_DIM = 128 the floor rejects 0 on 50% to 65% of the elements at N_CTX = 128 and on 11% to 29% at N_CTX = 1024, and on 11% of the causal ones at 4096, where tolO rejects none. The rest comes from Num.DotE5m2's constants: the score's relDot8 128 (3.2% of sum|q*k|) inside each exponent makes pE = 2^expErr about 1.5 to 1.6 at the test's X of 12 to 14, and relDot8 64 (1.57% of |acc|) compounds over the row's blocks. (2) The benchmark's data (randn, sm_scale = 1.3): tolO is 14 to 22 at HEAD_DIM = 64 and 1.4e4 to 2.0e4 at HEAD_DIM = 128 (X about 138), against |attnRef| <= 4; the floor would reject 0 on about 95% of the elements; tolM is 6.6 (log2 units) at HEAD_DIM = 128. (3) Larger N_CTX: for q = 0, v = 1 (attnRef = 1) tolO is 1.25 at N_CTX = 4096 (0 meets Post), 17.8 at 2^14 (the benchmark's largest) and 9.7e5 at 2^16 (Inst.ok.n_le); on test-like data at 2^16 it is 2.4e5 against |attnRef| about 0.002. The README's 'So the bound is meaningful on the test's shapes and data (0.14 to 1.04 at N <= 4096, against the test's own atol = 3)' measures the bound against the test's threshold, which is itself too loose to see that most heads read zeros. What is meaningful at every covered size: no fault, every element written and finite, nothing else written, the heads without vIn pinned to +-0 (tolO about 2^-17), and tolM at HEAD_DIM = 64 (about 0.2). What would resolve it: (a) a sharper library fact for the fp8 tl.dot (my LIBRARY_REPORT on Num.DotE5m2) and a correspondingly tighter tolO; or (b) the write-up saying plainly, in Specification and in Narrowings, where Post's accuracy part does not separate o from 0: the test's data at HEAD_DIM = 128 and most HEAD_DIM = 64 elements, the benchmark's data, and rows with values spread over the blocks at N_CTX >= 4096, growing as (1 + rhoA)^(N_CTX/64) to about 1e6 at the covered 2^16, in place of 'meaningful on the test's shapes and data'. With (b) I would release a DEFERRED response: the kernel's real use (the test's atol = 3) asks for no more, and narrowing N_CTX would not help, since the bound is already loose at the host's 2^14.
findings.evidence: work/tolerance.py and work/tolerance.out (the formulas of Model.lean evaluated row by row; the q = 0, v = 1 rows reproduce the README's own 0.46, 1.25 and 17.8, and the test-like D = 64 and D = 128 rows at N = 4096 its 0.30 and 1.04)

findings.summary: DotE5m2's relDot8 charges every fp8 tl.dot 2^-7 per chunk of |acc| too; fed back once per block it compounds as (1+relDot8 64)^T, so fp8 attention claims get no usable tolerance
findings.detail: Not a doubt of the fact's truth; a request for a sharper statement if the library's evidence supports one. docs/rules/num.md's chunk model says each wgmma instruction keeps 13 bits below the largest term, the accumulator included, and bounds a chunk by 33*2^-13 of the magnitudes' sum, which DotAcc applies to |acc| + sum|a*b| at every call. A kernel that feeds its accumulator back through tl.dot(p, v, acc) once per key block (tutorial 06's _attn_fwd here; any fp8 K loop with maxImpreciseAcc = 2^30) can then prove only a bound growing as (1 + relDot8 64)^T: 2.7 at T = 64, 54 at T = 256, 8.5e6 at T = 1024 (attn_fwd_e5m2's tolO is 9.7e5 for q = 0, v = 1 at N_CTX = 2^16). And the score's relDot8(D)*sum|q*k|, inside an exponent, multiplies each softmax weight by up to 2^(1.5*relDot8(D)*X), about 1.5 on the test's data at D = 128. Since by the same chunk model a product loses at most its own magnitude when truncated and the accumulator only its own truncation, a fact giving per instruction, for example, the smaller of the present bound and sum|a*b| + 2^-13*|acc| would bound such loops by about the sum of the terms' magnitudes, instead of a factor that grows without limit, and would let fp8 attention claims reject a zero output where the fp8 roundings alone allow it (attn_fwd_e5m2, finding on item:spec).

findings.summary: Say up front (README's opening, kernel.json's title, which kernels/README.md lists) that the claim certifies output 0 for every head with bh*HEAD_DIM >= Z*H: all but ceil(Z*H/HEAD_DIM) heads
findings.detail: I checked vEff against the source, the model and SEMANTICS.md's descriptor semantics myself and agree: line 98 reads v through the [HEAD_DIM, Z*H*N_CTX] descriptor at column bh*N_CTX*HEAD_DIM + j, inside it exactly when bh*HEAD_DIM < Z*H, all or nothing per head, and for those heads the address e*N_CTX + column is v's element (bh*HEAD_DIM + e)*N_CTX + j; the other heads read the zero padding, on both descriptor kinds (make_descV). Post states this honestly. But the write-up says it only in the Specification's fourth paragraph, the root module's docstring says 'the exact attention of the values the kernel uses', and the title is 'Fused attention, tutorial 06 (_attn_fwd, float8e5)': a reader of the kernel list would take the certificate for fp8 attention. On the host's shapes only 1 to 3 heads of a launch get attention over v (1 of 2 up to 3 of 192 in the test; 2 of 128 at HEAD_DIM = 64 and 1 of 128 at 128 in the benchmark). Stating it in the first lines (and the title) would keep the certificate from being read as more than it is.

notes: The model, the map and the launch agree with the source line by line by SEMANTICS.md on every covered instance (both descriptor kinds, both STAGE values, Z or H equal to 1); every name of the model prints as a TVA constant or a Model.lean helper (work/names.out, work/names2.out), the operator instances are TVA's, and main, consistent and satisfiable use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound (work/axioms.out). The host's inputs meet HeadOk's cap with overwhelming probability: by a Chernoff bound on the exact moment generating function of the float8e5 products, a benchmark pair at HEAD_DIM = 128 exceeds it with probability at most 1e-19.8, against 3.4e10 pairs in the largest launch (work/score_cap.out); the test's inputs are far below it.
